subject: Compatibility bridge & soft-landing ops for upcoming model contract
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Park <linda@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compatibility bridge & soft-landing ops for upcoming model contract

Hi Linda —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Based on Acme's timing, we understand you need a migration path for the v2027 model cutover that preserves current latency/quality SLAs for a 60-day window while you validate inference outputs.

To be explicit, we're proposing a two-track plan: 1) a short-term compatibility bridge (runtime shim + pin to compatible quantized variant) that keeps API contracts identical for callers, and 2) a soft-landing period where requests are routed to the new model variant behind a feature flag while we run side-by-side evaluation and QA.

High-level asks from our side to make this smooth: 
- Confirm the cutover target date (your PM mentioned mid-November).
- Any contract or procurement milestones required for the reserved compatibility window.
- A list of customer-internal endpoints that cannot tolerate >5% token-delta for output (helps us scope regression checks).

We can ship a compatibility checklist and canned customer comms (see attached draft) and allocate a small canary pool for Acme on Redwood Dedicated if you want guaranteed throughput.

Attaching a one-page checklist and a template comms doc for your legal/procurement. Happy to set a follow-up with Karthik (eng) and Laura (CS) to walk through implementation and timeline.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: compat-bridge-checklist.xlsx (stub), customer-comm-template.docx (stub)

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear proposal. Acme can commit to a mid-November cutover (current target: 2026-11-18). Procurement will need a short addendum to the current MSA that covers the 60-day compatibility window and defines success criteria for rollback vs. full switch.

Two immediate asks from our side: 
1) A formal checklist we can share with procurement (items like audit logs retention, KV cache isolation assurances, and SLA on latency during canary).
2) A one-page technical note for our eng leads describing the soft-landing routing behavior so they can prepare integration tests.

If you can provide those artifacts by next Wednesday (2026-10-28), procurement will start the addendum review and we can lock dates. Also looping in our procurement alias for transparency.

Best,

Thanks Vanessa — quick tech note draft below (happy to iterate). Sharing a short ops play we should include with the checklist so Acme's engs know what to expect.

-- tech note (one page) summary: 
1) Routing: we will support a feature-flagged route header (X-RDW-Canary) that directs a percentage of traffic to the new model variant. Default: 5% for first 48 hours, then 25% for next 7 days if regression metrics pass.
2) Regression criteria: token-level delta, latency tail (p95), and a small set of deterministic prompt IDs (Acme to provide list). Thresholds: token-delta < 5%, p95 latency within 20% of baseline.
3) KV cache handling: soft-landing will preserve prefix KV cache; we will avoid aggressive eviction during canary.
4) Rollback: automated route switch to prior runtime if regression thresholds breached for >3 hours.

-- ops play (checklist items relevant to eng): 
- Provide list of sensitive endpoints + deterministic prompts (due 2026-11-01)
- Confirm whether Acme wants sticky routing (session affinity) during canary
- Agree SLAs for canary throughput (we can reserve 2x baseline capacity for first 72 hours)

I'll attach the one-pager and a minimal routing-snippet example (curl + header). Marcus/Rishi, I left blank spots in the checklist for the legal/procurement language you will add.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Product Infra

Attachments: rdw-soft-landing-onepager.pdf (stub)
